title: Geometric integrality and genus of a smooth plane hypersurface
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $d\geq1$ an integer, and $F\in k[A,B,C]$ a nonzero homogeneous polynomial of degree $d$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put $Z=\operatorname{Proj}(k[A,B,C]/(F))\subset\mathbf P^2_k$ with its closed subscheme structure [def-pc-proj, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume that $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth of relative dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For every field extension $L/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], the base change $Z_L$ is the closed plane hypersurface of the coefficient image of $F$, the scalar map $L\to\Gamma(Z_L,\mathcal O_{Z_L})$ is an isomorphism, and $Z_L$ is nonempty and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. The scheme $Z$ is geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and every local ring of every $Z_L$ is an integrally closed domain. Thus $Z_L$ is a smooth H-projective geometrically integral curve [def-kun-projective], and its genus [def-pc-genus] is
$$g(Z_L)=\dim_LH^1(Z_L,\mathcal O_{Z_L})=(d-1)(d-2)/2.$$
Here $H^1$ is structure-sheaf cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. No rational point or algebraic closedness hypothesis on $k$ or $L$ is imposed.

proof.text: Fix any field extension $L/k$ and let $F_L$ be the coefficient image of $F$. A nonzero coefficient stays nonzero under the injective map $k\to L$, so $F_L$ is nonzero homogeneous of degree $d$. Apply [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary] to the graded quotient algebra. The graded isomorphism $L\otimes_k(k[A,B,C]/(F))\cong L[A,B,C]/(F_L)$ sends $l\otimes\bar P$ to $l\overline{P_L}$. Its inverse sends $l$ to $l\otimes1$ and each variable $X$ to $1\otimes\bar X$; it kills $F_L$ since its image is $1\otimes\bar F=0$. Both composites fix scalars and variables. This identifies $Z_L$ with that Proj. The canonical closed immersion into $\mathbf P^2_L$ is supplied by [lem-sfb-projective-hypersurface-structure-sequence] with $n=2$.

source.place: Tags 01NT (lemma-proj-base-change), 01O3 (lemma-relative-proj-base-change); curves.tex Tag 0BYD, quotient closed immersion

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-plane-hypersurface-cohomology] to $L,F_L,d$. Its hypotheses hold by step 1, and it gives the actual scalar isomorphism $L\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(Z_L,\mathcal O_{Z_L})$ and $\dim_LH^1(Z_L,\mathcal O_{Z_L})=(d-1)(d-2)/2$. This applies to every $L/k$ without a rational-point assumption.

The empty scheme has zero global-section ring, whereas step 2 gives the nonzero field $L$, so $Z_L$ is nonempty. If $Z_L=U\amalg V$ with both opens nonempty, glue the section $0$ on $U$ to $1$ on $V$. It is an idempotent global section distinct from both $0$ and $1$: at a point of either open its germ is evaluated in a nonzero local ring. Under step 2 it would give a nontrivial idempotent of $L$, impossible since $e(e-1)=0$ in a field. Thus $Z_L$ is connected.

source.place: Tag 0BYD, H0 conclusion; explicit elementary idempotent argument

proof.text: By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1), $Z_L\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is smooth of relative dimension one. For every field extension $M/L$, [def-pc-base-change] identifies $(Z_L)_M$ with $Z_M$; step 3 for the composite $M/k$ makes it connected. Hence $Z_L$ is geometrically connected over $L$ by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-connected-generic-geometry-core] to $Z_L\to\operatorname{Spec}L$. Its base is integral with integrally closed field local ring. Nonemptiness is step 3; smoothness is step 4. The sole fibre is $Z_L$, geometrically connected by step 4, so the fibre hypothesis holds. The generic fibre over the field base is $Z_L$ itself. The lemma gives that $Z_L$ is integral and every local ring is an integrally closed domain. Since $L/k$ was arbitrary, $Z$ is geometrically integral; applying this to all composites $M/k$ gives geometric integrality of each $Z_L$.

source.place: Tag 056T, lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal; existing normal integral geometry core, specialized to a field

proof.text: The closed immersion of step 1 is into $\operatorname{Proj}(L[A,B,C])$; applying [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary] to $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and the graded algebra $\mathbf Z[A,B,C]$ identifies this Proj over $\operatorname{Spec}L$ with $\mathbf P(\{0,1,2\};\operatorname{Spec}L)$, so $Z_L\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is H-projective by [def-kun-projective]. By [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper] it is proper, hence separated and of finite type, in particular quasi-compact, so $Z_L$ is projective over $L$ in the convention of [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve]. Step 4 gives smoothness of relative dimension one; since $\operatorname{Spec}L$ is a point, the only fibre is $Z_L$ itself, so $\dim_xZ_L=1$ at every $x$ and $\dim Z_L=1$. With the integrality of step 5, $Z_L$ is a curve over $L$, a smooth projective curve [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve], and geometrically irreducible because it is geometrically integral (step 5). Its genus is defined by [def-pc-genus] as $\dim_LH^1(Z_L,\mathcal O_{Z_L})$, already computed in step 2. This proves every assertion for every $L/k$.
